formats.reference: freedom-browser at meta.freedomBrowserCommit (integration/rust-core, the swarm reference's checkout), its src/main/wallet/ledger/signer.js, transport.js, errors.js, ipc.js and account-checks.js and identity-manager.js's addLedgerWallet, loaded fresh for each case with Electron stubbed, over meta.packages exactly (hw-app-eth builds every APDU). TransportNodeHid.open hands transport.js a recording transport, a subclass of the Transport class hw-transport-node-hid's transport extends (hw-transport 6.35.5, -noevents' copy), so send's framing, its 255-byte limit and its status check are the package's. No case reaches the network.
formats.device: the scripted device (generator/ledger-device.js) holds keys.json's abandon-12 mnemonic. E0 02: 65 ‖ the uncompressed key at the path (65 bytes) ‖ 40 ‖ its EIP-55 address without 0x (40 ASCII) ‖ 9000. B0 01: `device.b001` with the case's app. A transaction: 9000 until the RLP it was sent is whole, then v ‖ r ‖ s ‖ 9000 over keccak256 of the bytes after the path, v the parity for a typed one and (chainId' · 2 + 35 + parity) mod 256 for type 0, chainId' the chain ID's first four bytes. A message: 9000 until it has the announced length, then 27 + parity ‖ r ‖ s over its EIP-191 hash. E0 1A and E0 1C: 9000 (6D00 for a device with `fields: false`, a Nano S). E0 0C 00 01: a signature over the case's `expected_hash` (the device can't hash fields; LDG-3's recordings check that a real one gets the same hash); E0 0C 00 00 over keccak256(19 01 ‖ the two hashes). Every signature is RFC 6979's, low s. `fault`: at APDU `at` (0-based, the case's) the device answers `status` alone, or throws DisconnectedDeviceDuringOperation (node-hid's read failure). `answer_fault` at APDU `at` (`signature`: the APDU the device signs at): other-address (another seed's key and address), key-not-address (the path's address text beside another key), other-key (keys.json's account 1 signs), other-digest (a signature over keccak256 of the digest), high-s (n − s, the parity flipped), flip-v (the parity flipped), long (one byte more), short (one byte less), v-27 (27 + parity for a type 0). `open`: no-device (the transport's own TransportError NoDevice), cannot-open (node-hid's "cannot open device with path").
formats.case: { id, family, operation (the core's method), request (the core's wire form: ledger.accounts { scheme, start, count }; ledger.add { name, address, path }, the reference's wallet:add-ledger-wallet arguments; sign.transaction { tx } in 0002's form; sign.message { message } the bytes; sign.typed_data { typed_data, expected_hash }, the hash the user confirmed, over which the reference recovers), record { path, address } for a signature, x402 { version, requirements, now_s, nonce } where @x402/evm 2.29.0 built the typed data under that clock and nonce, device (above), fault_step (the step a fault is at), exchanges [{ apdu, answer } | { apdu, thrown: { name, message } }] in order (hex), transport { opened, closed }, events (the record's address check as onAddressCheck heard it, the core call addLedgerWallet made, the reference's console), result, deviation, also }. result: { status: success, accounts, mismatched } for discovery (ipc.js's answer), { status: success, wallet } for an add, { status: success, raw | signature | payload }, or { status: error, code, message, cause }.
formats.deviation: a case the core answers differently names its deviation (design 0016's table) in `deviation`, and any other in `also`; the result is the reference's. `deviations` lists each Ledger deviation with its cases, or why none can show it. ledger-grammar.json gives the core's stream for each case (`honest`) or its refusal (`refused`).
formats.typed_data_excluded: 0002's typed-data cases ethers and the core sign that no Ledger case carries, and why.

device.b001: format 01, the name, the version, flags 01 00, then 9000

device-deadlines.note: no case: the reference sets no deadline (hw-transport's 15 s only emits "unresponsive"); LDG-2 tests both deadlines under a fixed clock

cancel.note: no case: the reference has no way to cancel an exchange; LDG-2 cancels before the first APDU, between two and during the user's wait

discovery-busy.note: no case: it needs discovery while a signature holds the device queue, which one case's run never does; LDG-2's lane tests make it

typed_data_excluded.why: the device rebuilds M(uint8[2] v), the hash has M(uint8[02] v)
